summary: The SPHEREx Transient Detector is an automated pipeline that scans deep-space telescope images to catch sudden cosmic events like supernovas or moving asteroids. Using Python, Astropy, and NumPy, the system processes raw FITS sky surveys, aligns before-and-after exposures into standardized cutouts, and generates side by side comparisons to highlight changes. A Convolutional Neural Network built in PyTorch then analyzes those aligned pairs to separate genuine astrophysical transients from visual noise, while an interactive Streamlit and HTML/JS web dashboard displays the results for human review.
details: The SPHEREx Transient Detector is an automated pipeline that scans deep-space telescope imagery to spot sudden cosmic events like supernovas or moving asteroids. Built with Python, Astropy, and NumPy, it ingests raw FITS sky surveys, aligns before-and-after exposures to eliminate false triggers from telescope drift, and generates side by side images for visual comparison. A Convolutional Neural Network trained in PyTorch on an NVIDIA RTX 4060 Ti analyzes these aligned cutouts to separate genuine astrophysical transients from sensor noise, while an interactive Streamlit and HTML/JS dashboard presents the results for human inspection. By automating heavy data cleaning and compressing massive sky surveys into lightweight cutouts, the tool bridges rigorous scientific precision with an accessible, creative interface—cutting discovery analysis from hours of manual review down to seconds so researchers and students can flag high-interest celestial anomalies effortlessly.
